The failing test `testAddNaN` in the `ComplexTest` class of the `org.apache.commons.math.complex` package is testing the `add` method of the `Complex` class. The test creates a `Complex` number with a NaN value and adds it to another `Complex` number.

The current bug report highlights a discrepancy in how NaN values are handled in the `add` and `subtract` methods of the `Complex` class. The Javadoc for both methods states that if either `this` or `rhs` has a NaN value in either part, `NaN` should be returned. However, there seems to be a discrepancy in the implementation between `add` and `subtract` methods in handling NaN values.

Inspecting the code snippet of the `add` method in the `Complex` class, we see that the method simply performs addition on the real and imaginary parts of the complex numbers without explicitly handling NaN values. This might be the reason for the observed difference in behavior between the `add` and `subtract` methods when NaN values are involved.

To address this issue, we need to ensure that the `add` method follows the same NaN handling logic as the `subtract` method when performing arithmetic operations involving NaN values.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
The likely fix for this issue would be to update the `add` method in the `Complex` class to handle NaN values consistently with the `subtract` method. 

The method that needs to be fixed is:
```
org.apache.commons.math.complex.Complex.add(org.apache.commons.math.complex.Complex)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
